title: Vite Web Development
description: Beginner-to-advanced Vite reference covering project setup, native-ESM development, configuration, environments, assets, CSS, plugins, dependency optimization, production builds, libraries, SSR, testing, and deployment.

sections.title: Project & Development Server
sections.description: Understand Vite's source-oriented development model and entry points.

subtopics.title: Create a Project & CLI
subtopics.description: Vite serves source modules during development and produces an optimized deployment build. Framework templates add their official integration plugin.

codeBlocks.code:
npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev
npm run build
npm run preview

# Direct CLI
npx vite --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173
npx vite build --mode staging

callouts.title: preview Is Not a Production Server
callouts.text: vite preview locally checks built output. Deploy dist through a production static host/CDN or the server runtime required by your framework.

subtopics.title: index.html, Root & Entry Graph
subtopics.description: index.html is source and part of the module graph, not a passive public-file template. Module script URLs resolve from the configured root/base.

callouts.title: public Is Escape-Hatch Storage
callouts.text: Files in public are copied unchanged and referenced from root paths. Prefer imported assets when hashing, dependency tracking, or missing-file diagnostics are useful.

subtopics.title: Native ESM & Hot Module Replacement
subtopics.description: Development transforms modules on demand and invalidates affected graph nodes. Framework plugins preserve component state only when refresh boundaries remain valid.

callouts.title: HMR Is Development Semantics
callouts.text: Always test clean reloads and production builds. Module side effects, stale singleton state, and refresh behavior can hide initialization bugs.

sections.title: Configuration & Module Resolution
sections.description: Keep configuration typed, portable, and explicit about mode-dependent behavior.

subtopics.title: vite.config & defineConfig
subtopics.description: Configuration may be an object or function receiving command/mode. Use loadEnv when config itself needs mode files.

callouts.title: Config Runs in Node
callouts.text: vite.config executes in the tooling runtime, while application modules run in browser/SSR environments. Do not import browser-only source into config.

subtopics.title: Aliases, Dedupe & Resolution Conditions
subtopics.description: Aliases should use absolute filesystem replacements. Dedupe forces one package copy; conditional exports select environment-specific package entry points.

callouts.title: Align TypeScript Paths
callouts.text: Editor/type-checker aliases and Vite resolution are separate unless integrated. Configure both or use an appropriate plugin; test production resolution.

subtopics.title: Dev Server Proxy, CORS & Host
subtopics.description: Proxy API paths during development to avoid browser cross-origin setup while preserving a stable frontend URL contract.

callouts.title: Development Proxy Is Not Deployment
callouts.text: Configure the production reverse proxy/API origin separately. Do not expose the dev server broadly or disable host/CORS protections without understanding network risk.

sections.title: Environment, Assets & CSS
sections.description: Know which values become public build output and which files enter the dependency graph.

subtopics.title: import.meta.env & Modes
subtopics.description: Vite statically replaces built-ins and exposed prefixes. Mode selects .env files; it is distinct from NODE_ENV.

table.title: Vite Environment File Priority
rows: Set in shell or CI secret store
Commit non-secret mode defaults if useful
All modes except Vite's test conventions may vary by runner

callouts.title: VITE_ Values Are Public
callouts.text: Exposed variables are bundled into client code. Never place secrets, private tokens, or server credentials in them; use a backend/secret manager.

subtopics.title: Imported Assets, URLs & Workers
subtopics.description: Imported assets receive hashed deployment URLs. new URL with import.meta.url supports relative assets; worker constructors are statically analyzed.

callouts.title: Dynamic URL Analysis Is Limited
callouts.text: Arbitrary runtime strings cannot always be discovered at build time. Use import.meta.glob or an explicit map for finite dynamic assets/modules.

subtopics.title: CSS, Modules & Preprocessors
subtopics.description: CSS imports participate in HMR/build extraction. CSS Modules provide locally scoped class mappings; supported preprocessors require their compiler package.

callouts.title: Order Still Matters
callouts.text: Scope prevents class-name collisions, not cascade/order issues. Define layers/tokens and avoid depending on incidental import order across code-split chunks.

sections.title: Plugins & Dependency Optimization
sections.description: Extend the pipeline deliberately and understand development pre-bundling.

subtopics.title: Plugin Selection & Ordering
subtopics.description: Vite plugins extend Rollup-compatible hooks plus dev-server features. Use official/framework-maintained plugins and limit conditional application with apply/enforce.

callouts.title: Plugins Execute Trusted Code
callouts.text: A plugin runs during development/build with filesystem and environment access. Review ownership, permissions, dependencies, and update changes.

subtopics.title: Custom Plugin Hooks & Virtual Modules
subtopics.description: Use resolveId/load for virtual modules and transform for source changes. Prefix internal resolved virtual IDs with a null byte convention.

callouts.title: Return Source Maps
callouts.text: Transform plugins that change line/column positions should return accurate source maps so debugging and error locations remain useful.

subtopics.title: Dependency Pre-Bundling & Linked Packages
subtopics.description: Development pre-bundles dependencies for CommonJS/ESM compatibility and request efficiency. Source/linked packages may need include, exclude, dedupe, or correct package metadata.

callouts.title: Do Not Cargo-Cult optimizeDeps
callouts.text: Add overrides only for diagnosed packages. Verify workspace packages declare ESM/CJS and exports correctly rather than relying on permanent cache resets.

sections.title: Production Builds & Deployment
sections.description: Control base paths, chunking, compatibility, source maps, and hosting fallback behavior.

subtopics.title: build, base & Output
subtopics.description: vite build emits hashed assets to outDir. base rewrites public paths for root, subpath, or relative deployment.

callouts.title: SPA Fallback Is Host Configuration
callouts.text: Client-side routes need unknown paths rewritten to index.html while real assets/404s remain correct. Configure CDN/server caching separately: immutable hashed assets, short-lived HTML.

subtopics.title: Code Splitting, Dynamic Import & Analysis
subtopics.description: Dynamic import creates asynchronous boundaries. Inspect build output before manually grouping chunks.

callouts.title: Chunking Is a Network Trade-off
callouts.text: Too few chunks overfetch; too many add requests and waterfalls. Measure initial bytes, cache reuse, and navigation latency before manualChunks changes.

subtopics.title: Browser Targets & Polyfills
subtopics.description: Build target controls syntax transformation, not every missing runtime API. Add polyfills based on an explicit support matrix.

callouts.title: Modern by Default
callouts.text: Supporting obsolete browsers increases JavaScript and testing cost. Define support from user/product data and use a legacy plugin only when justified.

sections.title: Library Mode, SSR & Advanced Environments
sections.description: Treat libraries and multi-environment applications as explicit output contracts.

subtopics.title: Library Mode & External Dependencies
subtopics.description: Library mode builds one or more public entry points. Externalize peer dependencies and publish types/exports/files deliberately.

callouts.title: Test the Packed Artifact
callouts.text: Use npm pack and install the tarball into ESM/CJS consumer fixtures. Source-workspace imports can hide missing files, bad exports, and duplicate peers.

subtopics.title: SSR Entry Points & Manifest
subtopics.description: SSR uses separate server/client entries; server rendering, asset preload, hydration, routing, and data serialization must agree.

codeBlocks.code:
vite build --outDir dist/client
vite build --ssr src/entry-server.ts --outDir dist/server

# Use --ssrManifest/manifest to map modules to emitted client assets.

callouts.title: Prefer a Framework for Product SSR
callouts.text: Bare Vite SSR is low-level. A framework handles routing, streaming, data, serialization, errors, and deployment integrations; do not improvise security-sensitive hydration payloads.

subtopics.title: Environment API & Version-Sensitive Features
subtopics.description: Advanced APIs can model client, SSR, worker, and custom runtimes with environment-specific graphs and plugin pipelines.

codeBlocks.code:
Use framework-supported environment configuration first.
Check current Vite stability and migration notes before adopting Environment API internals.
Plugin authors must avoid shared mutable state assumptions across environments/builds.
Test dev and build because environment pipelines can differ.

callouts.title: Check Stability Before Production
callouts.text: Environment and builder APIs have evolved across Vite majors. Pin Vite/plugins, read migration guides, and avoid undocumented internal server/module graph APIs.

sections.title: Testing, Troubleshooting & Checklist
sections.description: Separate transpilation from type checking and debug graph/cache/environment issues systematically.

subtopics.title: TypeScript, Testing & Quality Gates
subtopics.description: Vite transpiles TypeScript but does not perform full type checking. Run tsc and lint/tests separately; use a Vite-compatible test runner when sharing transforms.

callouts.title: Build Success Is Not Type Safety
callouts.text: A Vite build may succeed with TypeScript errors. CI must run the compiler and framework-specific type generation/checks explicitly.

subtopics.title: Common Failure Diagnosis
subtopics.description: Identify whether failure is resolution, transform, dependency optimization, HMR, environment, build, or host behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
Works after restart only → module side effect/HMR invalidation/env reload
Works in dev, fails build → dynamic import, SSR/browser boundary, case-sensitive path
Duplicate React/invalid hooks → multiple package copies; inspect lockfile + dedupe
Blank deployed subpath → base or host rewrite mismatch
Stale dependency → optimizer/browser cache; inspect before --force
Missing env → prefix/mode/priority/restart
Source-map location wrong → transform plugin map

subtopics.title: Vite 8: Rolldown, Oxc & Migration
subtopics.description: Vite 8 uses Rolldown as the unified bundler and Oxc-based tooling while retaining broad Rollup plugin compatibility. Review renamed options and behavioral differences instead of assuming a drop-in major upgrade.

callouts.title: Audit Rollup and esbuild Options
callouts.text: Rollup-compatible hooks remain useful, but Vite 8 migrations should review rolldownOptions, dependency optimization, transform behavior, Node support, plugin compatibility, and removed or deprecated esbuild-era settings.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Validate toolchain trust, environment exposure, output paths, browser support, and deployment semantics.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Node/Vite/plugin versions and lockfile are pinned
□ Type checking, linting, tests, and build run independently
□ Client env contains no secrets
□ Aliases match TypeScript/editor resolution
□ Dynamic imports/assets are statically discoverable
□ base and SPA/server routing match the host
□ HTML and hashed-asset cache headers differ correctly
□ Bundle/chunk output is measured
□ Browser targets and polyfills match support policy
□ Source maps follow disclosure policy
□ Plugins are reviewed as privileged build code
□ SSR/client boundaries and serialization are tested
□ Packed libraries are tested from emitted artifacts
